task.name: What an issue cost across all its attempts is never reported, so the figure that should decide whether to re-run it is the one an operator cannot see
task.story_text:
## Why

Every cost an operator is shown is scoped to a run. What an issue cost to land is never reported
anywhere, and for the issues that matter most it is the only figure that describes what happened.

An issue that fails, is preserved, and is re-entered accrues spend across several runs. Each run
reports its own total honestly, and the per-run records sum correctly — the arithmetic is sound.
What is missing is the sum. Status output, sprint summaries and the RCA all stop at the run
boundary, so the number that answers "what did this issue cost" exists only by querying the audit
substrate directly.

The gap is not evenly distributed. Measured over roughly two weeks of this project's own history:

```
runs to land   issues   avg total   sum
     1           80      $12.61     $1,008.95
     2           12      $19.35       $232.22
     3+           4     $117.43       $469.71
```

17% of issues needed more than one run and consumed 41% of all spend. Four issues — 4% of the work —
accounted for 27% of the total. An issue needing three runs costs roughly nine times one that lands
first time.

None of that is visible while it is happening. The largest single one reached $341 across five runs,
and the biggest figure ever displayed for it was $169.94, on a screen that described a run rather
than the issue. An operator watching per-run costs sees numbers that look survivable while the
actual commitment compounds out of view, and the decision that figure should inform — keep re-running
this, or stop and re-scope it — is exactly the decision being made without it.

The routing layer already reasons in these terms: a story allocation is derived from historical
per-story cost, and escalation messages quote medians and percentiles over prior runs. So the
aggregate exists internally as an input to automated decisions. It is simply never surfaced to the
person paying for it.

## Example

What is shown today while an issue is re-entered for the fifth time, and what is not:

```
shown                                   not shown
─────────────────────────────────       ──────────────────────────────
run 7b995cfaaa5f   $137.69              issue total        $341.10
elapsed 2h 43m                          runs to date             5
sprint total       $166.81              elapsed, all runs   ~9h 20m
                                        outcomes    RC, APPROVE, RC, killed, escalated
```

Wanted: at the point an issue is re-entered, and in any summary that names it, the figure for the
issue alongside the figure for the run — so a fifth attempt is visibly a fifth attempt, and its
running total is on screen when the decision to make it is taken.

## Acceptance criteria

- A surface that names an issue reports what that issue has cost across every run that worked on it,
  not only the run being displayed, so the aggregate never has to be reconstructed by hand.
- The aggregate counts each run's spend once. Where a run already carries spend forward from an
  earlier attempt, the total reflects what was spent, not the sum of figures that overlap.
- Where any run contributing to the total recorded unmeasured spend, the aggregate says so rather
  than presenting a total that silently understates itself.
- The count of attempts is reported with the cost, so an operator can tell a single expensive attempt
  from several cheap ones, which call for different responses.
- An issue re-entered after a previous attempt has its running total available at the point of
  re-entry, before the new attempt spends anything.
- An issue that has only ever run once reads the same as it does today, so the common case gains a
  figure rather than changing meaning.

## Out of scope

Changing what is spent, or how allocation is derived from history. This is a reporting gap: the
records already exist and already sum correctly. Also out of scope is recording what a run changed
as opposed to what it cost, which is tracked separately.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 counts only audit_records already present, while coordinator/run_setup.py:_setup_resume_entry creates the new run ID before its audit row exists. At re-entry, an issue beginning its fifth attempt could therefore display four attempts unless Step 4 distinguishes completed attempts from the current attempt ordinal.
  Suggestion: In run setup, render the aggregate's completed-attempt count together with the new ordinal, for example 'issue total $X across 4 prior attempts; entering attempt 5', or overlay the newly created run ID with zero spend before displaying it.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 detects incompleteness solely via total_cost_usd IS NULL, but cost_complete is absent from the coordinator layer — grep finds it only in sprint/ and cli/, with zero hits in src/theforge/coordinator/. Per sprint/unmeasured.py, an *accepted* unmeasured source keeps cost_complete false while the measured total stays a lower bound, so a contributing run can carry a numeric total that still understates. Step 4's re-entry path reads the substrate directly with no sprint-summary overlay, so it is the surface least able to see that signal.
  Suggestion: Have the Step 1 helper read the completeness signal out of the record's raw_json (which audit_substrate already stores and migrates via _load_migrated) rather than inferring it only from a NULL column, and add a Step 6 case for a run with a numeric total but incomplete cost.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 says the re-entry display should 'load the issue aggregate for the slug', but Step 1 keys the aggregate by issue_id. reentry_display.load_reentry_display/reentry_lines take a slug, and audit_records carries both columns, so a resolution step is needed between them.
  Suggestion: Give the Step 1 helper the same slug/issue_id selector shape latest_record_for already uses (audit_substrate.py:2354-2373), so slug-keyed callers resolve without a separate lookup; omit the line when neither identifier is available.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Preflight flagged src/theforge/sprint/unmeasured.py as a likely file, but no step touches it. This is acceptable as written since AC3 is served through the NULL/summary-block path, though the accepted-ceiling representation lives there.
  Suggestion: If the dev finds the completeness signal needs normalizing, reuse unmeasured.normalize_source_id / partition rather than re-deriving acceptance semantics in the substrate layer.

findings.description: The story narrative targets specific places where the aggregate should appear ('at the point an issue is re-entered' and 'in any summary that names it'), but AC1 broadens this to 'a surface that names an issue'. That phrase is unbounded and makes it unclear which screens, logs, or reports are actually in scope.

AC3 is orphaned from the stated problem. The Why/Example sections describe missing cross-run totals, but they do not introduce 'unmeasured spend' as a requirement or define how that condition is surfaced. This adds a new behavior without corresponding story justification.

AC6 is ambiguous as written: 'reads the same as it does today' is time-relative and subjective. Reviewers cannot verify what must remain unchanged for single-run issues beyond a general intent not to change meaning.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Add one audit-substrate issue-cost aggregate and make every issue-naming surface consume that same shape. Keep per-run cost displays intact, adding issue-level total and attempt count beside them, with incomplete totals rendered as lower bounds when any contributing run was unmeasured.

steps.description: Add a canonical issue-level cost aggregate over audit records.
steps.details: Add a read-only helper near `latest_record_for` that selects `audit_records` by `issue_id`, orders by `started_at`, counts distinct `run_id` values as attempts, sums numeric `total_cost_usd` as the measured lower bound, and marks the aggregate incomplete when any contributing row has `total_cost_usd IS NULL`. Base the aggregate on per-run audit records, not accumulated sprint rows; use the existing `prior_generation.independently_recorded` convention so carried prior spend is not counted again when its parent run is already independently recorded.

steps.description: Persist and propagate the aggregate in sprint artifacts that name stories.
steps.details: When writing `sprint-summary.yaml` story rows, attach an `issue_cost` block for issue-backed stories with total/measured cost, cost completeness, attempt count, and contributing run ids; overlay the current summary row when the current run is not yet present in the substrate. In RCA generation, include the same block beside the existing per-story `cost_accounting` so the RCA reports issue-level spend without redoing arithmetic.

steps.description: Render issue totals in live and completed sprint status rows.
steps.details: Extend `StoryStatusEntry` with optional issue-cost fields populated from the summary block when present or from the substrate plus current live row otherwise. Keep the existing per-run `COST` column unchanged, and add a subordinate line such as `issue total: $X across N attempt(s)`; when incomplete, render the measured lower bound with the existing unknown/lower-bound wording rather than a confident total.

steps.description: Show prior issue spend at re-entry before new work starts.
steps.details: Have the shared re-entry display load the issue aggregate for the slug and emit an `issue total` line with attempts before the outstanding/re-entry lines. Also log the same aggregate from resume setup before recovered state can lead to additional spend, so `forge sprint --resume` and pending-decision status expose the running total at the decision point.

steps.description: Render issue totals in the completed sprint digest.
steps.details: Update `_story_row` and outstanding/failure sections to use the persisted `issue_cost` block, falling back to dynamic lookup for older summaries. Preserve the existing row cost as the run cost and add issue total plus attempts only as an additional figure.

steps.description: Cover aggregation, rendering, unmeasured, and carry-forward behavior with focused tests.
steps.details: Add tests for multi-run measured aggregation, `NULL` run cost producing an incomplete issue aggregate, attempt counting, independently recorded carried spend not double-counting, summary/RCA payload fields, status/digest rendering, re-entry disclosure before new spend, and the one-attempt case where run cost and issue cost agree.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A surface that names an issue reports what that issue has cost across every run that worked on it, not only the run being displayed, so the aggregate never has to be reconstructed by hand.
The aggregate counts each run's spend once. Where a run already carries spend forward from an earlier attempt, the total reflects what was spent, not the sum of figures that overlap.
Where any run contributing to the total recorded unmeasured spend, the aggregate says so rather than presenting a total that silently understates itself.
The count of attempts is reported with the cost, so an operator can tell a single expensive attempt from several cheap ones, which call for different responses.
An issue re-entered after a previous attempt has its running total available at the point of re-entry, before the new attempt spends anything.
An issue that has only ever run once reads the same as it does today, so the common case gains a figure rather than changing meaning.

risks.description: Old sprint summaries will not contain the new `issue_cost` block.
risks.mitigation: Use dynamic substrate lookup as a fallback in status, digest, and RCA paths, and omit only when neither issue id nor audit history is available.

risks.description: The phrase 'worked on it' is ambiguous for zero-cost ALREADY_DONE or shape-skip rows.
risks.mitigation: Count only coordinator audit records for the issue as attempts; keep shape-skip event history out of issue spend because it is not a per-story run cost record.

risks.description: Current live runs may not yet be indexed in `audit_records`.
risks.mitigation: Overlay the current live/completed story row by run id before rendering, and skip the overlay when the substrate already contains that run.
